subject: ingles
titulo: Basic English Grammar Parts of Speech
contenido: A noun is a word that names a person, place, thing, or animal. Nouns can be singular or plural, formed using regular rules or irregular changes. A verb represents an action performed by a person, animal, or object. An adjective describes a noun and can use comparative or superlative forms to compare items.
ejemplos: The dog runs in the yard. 2. The small cat slept on the bed. 3. A dog is faster than an elephant.

ejercicios.subject: ingles
ejercicios.texto: Nouns can be singular or plural. A plural noun means there is more than one person, place, thing, or animal. Most plural nouns are formed by adding -s to the end of the singular noun, like turning book into books. However, if a noun ends in s, ch, sh, x, or z, we add -es to make it plural, such as changing box into boxes.

preguntas.enunciado: Which plural word is formed by adding -es because it ends in the letter x?
preguntas.pista: Boxes ends in x so it forms its plural by adding -es to the end

preguntas.enunciado: Most plural nouns are formed by adding -s to the end of the singular noun, like turning book into [___].
preguntas.pista: The plural form of book is books created by adding -s to the singular noun.

preguntas.enunciado: What suffix is added to a singular noun ending in s, ch, sh, x, or z to make it plural?
preguntas.pista: The suffix -es is added to singular nouns ending in s, ch, sh, x, or z

ejercicios.subject: ingles
ejercicios.texto: Irregular plural nouns do not follow standard rules, so you have to memorize them. Some irregular plural nouns change their spelling completely when they become plural. For example, man becomes men, tooth becomes teeth, child becomes children, and mouse becomes mice. Other irregular nouns stay exactly the same in plural form, such as sheep, fish, pants, and scissors.

preguntas.enunciado: For example, man becomes men, tooth becomes teeth, child becomes [___], and mouse becomes mice.
preguntas.pista: Children is the irregular plural form of child with a spelling change.

preguntas.enunciado: Which plural noun stays exactly the same as its singular form without changing spelling?
preguntas.pista: Sheep remains identical in both singular and plural forms without adding suffixes or changing spelling

preguntas.enunciado: What singular noun changes its spelling to become "mice" in its plural form?
preguntas.pista: Mouse changes its spelling to mice in the irregular plural form

ejercicios.subject: ingles
ejercicios.texto: We use comparative adjectives to compare two things, like saying a dog is faster than an elephant. We use superlative adjectives to show something is the most or best among a group, such as stating the dog is the fastest. For one-syllable adjectives, we add -er to form the comparative and -est to form the superlative. Some adjectives are irregular, changing good to better and best.

preguntas.enunciado: In the sentence "A dog is faster than an elephant", what type of adjective is "faster"?
preguntas.pista: Faster compares two animals directly using the suffix -er and the word than

preguntas.enunciado: We use superlative adjectives to show something is the [___] or best among a group.
preguntas.pista: Superlative adjectives indicate that something possesses a quality to the most extreme degree.

preguntas.enunciado: What is the comparative form of the irregular adjective "good"?
preguntas.pista: Better is the irregular comparative form of the adjective good
